articles.summary: Tools and Technology How to Conduct a Payroll Audit in Nigeria: A Step-by-Step Guide for Businesses Oluwakemi Adesina August 31, 2026 An effective Payroll Audit is essential in Nigerian businesses to detect calculation errors and compliance gaps before they trigger costly penalties from regulations. A payroll audit is just you checking your own work before someone else does it for you, and possibly less gently. When done well, it improves your accuracy, keeps you compliant, and gives your employees one less reason to worry on payday. If you’ve never done a full payroll audit, or it’s been a long time, take this as your reminder. Here’s how to do it, step by step. What Is a Payroll Audit? A payroll audit is a full review of your payroll records, processes, and controls. Who runs the audit and when it happens is important. An internal payroll audit is managed by your finance or HR team, on your own schedule, so you can catch errors early while they’re still easy to fix. An external audit happens when someone else, like an investor, acquirer, or PenCom and NRS, needs to review your records, often when your Pension Clearance Certificate is up for renewal. If you build strong payroll compliance ahead of time, an external audit will just be a routine check instead of a major problem. Payroll Reconciliation vs Payroll Audit in Nigeria These two terms are easily mixed up, but they’re not the same. Payroll reconciliation checks if this month’s payment matches what payroll calculated. It looks at hours, salary, deductions, and net pay, and compares them to the bank records. A payroll audit goes further and asks if you can trust the whole system that produces these numbers, and whether it would pass a regulator’s review. You need both processes. If you only do reconciliation, you’re just checking the math without looking at the bigger process. If you only do audits, you might review the big picture once a year, but small mistakes can add up in the meantime. Here’s what that pile-up actually costs. Say a company under-remits pension contributions by ₦150,000 a month because a new hire’s pension PIN was never activated. Reconciliation won’t catch it: the payslip math is consistent, the deduction shows, but it never reaches the PFA. After six months, that’s ₦900,000 unremitted. Under Section 11(6) of the Pension Reform Act 2014, the penalty is 2% of the outstanding amount per month of default. PenCom’s recovery agents have pulled over ₦32 billion from employers in this position since 2012. A quarterly payroll audit Nigeria businesses run properly would have caught that PIN in month one. If you under-remit pension by ₦150,000 a month because a new hire’s PIN was never activated, reconciliation won’t catch it. The payslip looks right, but the money never reaches the PFA. After six months, that’s ₦900,000 in unremitted funds. The penalty is at least 2% per month. PenCom has recovered over ₦32 billion from employers like this since 2012. A quarterly payroll audit would have caught the missing PIN in month one. Payroll Audit Nigeria Checklist Employee master records: Names, bank details, tax IDs, and pension PINs, checked against actual documentation, not what’s been sitting in the system since onboarding. Salary structures: Is everyone on the correct grade, with the right split for basic, housing, and transport? Overtime and bonuses: Approved before payment, calculated and taxed correctly, and documented, not just verbally agreed. Leave balances: Accurate, and not silently converted to cash without sign-off. Payroll reports. Reconciled against your general ledger and bank statements; if they don’t match, that gap is where you start digging. Tax deductions: Checked against the current PAYE bands, with the ₦800,000 tax-free threshold and ₦4,000 Development Levy applied, remitted by the 10th of the following month. Pension deductions: The statutory 8% employee and 10% employer contribution on Basic, Housing, and Transport, reaching the correct PFA within 7 working days, in line with PenCom‘s rules. NHF contributions: Confirmed against current requirements through the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria. Bank transfer records: Every payment traceable to an approved payroll run, no unexplained transfers. If your business has fewer than 50 employees, check every record. If you have more than 50, review a sample and pay special attention to new hires, recent salary changes, and anyone paid outside the usual payroll process. Common Payroll Risks Businesses Should Watch For An audit is only effective if you know what to look for. The same issues appear in nearly every payroll compliance audit: Duplicate employees: The same person was entered twice, resulting in two salaries. Ghost employees: Usually not fraud from day one; more often, an exit was never removed from the payroll file, or a contract staffer whose bank details stayed active after leaving. Incorrect salaries: Pay that doesn’t match the approved contract or latest revision. Incorrect deductions: Tax or pension calculated on outdated bands or the wrong salary base. Unauthorized payroll changes: A salary, bank account, or deduction edited by someone who shouldn’t have been able to. Poor documentation: Approvals that exist verbally but never on paper. Each of these problems might seem minor at first. But if you ignore them, any one can turn into a number your finance team can’t explain. Regular internal payroll audits help you catch these issues early. Payroll Controls That Support Successful Audits Good payroll controls do more than help you pass audits. They make audits quicker and easier to manage. Put these controls in place before you need them. Approval workflows: No salary, bonus, or bank detail change without documented sign-off. Segregation of duties: The person who processes payroll should not be the one to approve it as well. Most payroll fraud happens when one person handles both tasks. Payroll reports generated every cycle Audit trails: A record of who changed what, and when, for every payroll edit. Employee record verification: Checked at onboarding and periodically after, in line with Nigeria Data Protection Commission requirements. Make this a routine every payroll

articles.summary: Business Center HR Compliance Checklist in Nigeria: Essential Requirements Every Employer Should Know Oluwakemi Adesina August 31, 2026 While paperwork may not be the reason you started your business, maintaining HR compliance in Nigeria is essential to protect both your business and reputation. Monthly compliance involves managing contracts, tax deductions, and office policies. Missing any step can result in fines, loss of employee trust, regulatory scrutiny, or legal action. Fortunately, compliance can be manageable. The following guidance will help you protect your business, remain compliant, and support your employees. Why HR Compliance Matters Some founders believe HR rules only apply to larger teams, but compliance is required regardless of company size. Proactive compliance protects your business from the outset. Protects Employers and Employees: Clear policies ensure employees understand their terms and provide employers with protection against unfair claims. Reduces Legal and Operational Risks: A single labor dispute can drain your cash flow and destroy your reputation. Proper documentation keeps you out of court. Makes HR Operations faster: With structure in place, onboarding is quick, payroll takes minutes, and your team knows what to expect. What Is HR Compliance in Nigeria? HR compliance means meeting every rule for how you hire, pay, document, and manage your team. It covers everything from the first offer letter to the final payout. Why should every employer prioritize compliance from day one? Because employment compliance in Nigeria covers the entire employee lifecycle. You cannot simply hand over a handbook at onboarding and assume you are safe. Compliance is an ongoing operational habit. It continues through every leave request, salary review, policy update, and eventual exit. Employment Documentation Every Employer Should Maintain Maintain a secure and comprehensive HR compliance checklist for each employee, including these six essential documents: Employment Contracts: Written, signed documents specifying the exact role, salary, working hours, and termination terms. Update these formally whenever terms change. Offer Letters: The formal record of what you agreed to before day one. This is vital when disputes arise about what was initially promised. Employee Identification: Keep a verified government ID (NIN or passport) on file for every staff member. Emergency Contacts: Collect and update next-of-kin details periodically. Employee Records: A single file for job history, promotions, disciplinary actions, and performance reviews. Policy Acknowledgments: Signed confirmation that the employee has read, understood, and accepted your handbook. Payroll Compliance Requirements Payroll is where compliance meets your bank account. To meet your statutory employer obligations in Nigeria, you must coordinate with official agencies and get your numbers right. Focus on these four key areas for ongoing financial compliance: PAYE (Pay-As-You-Earn): Income tax must be calculated accurately based on current tax bands. You must deduct this monthly and remit it directly to the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) by the 10th day of the following month. Pension Contributions: In line with the National Pension Commission, you must handle the statutory 8% employee deduction and 10% employer contribution based on Basic, Housing, and Transport (BHT) figures. Remit these funds to the employee’s chosen PFA within 7 working days of paying salaries to avoid stiff penalties from PenCom. National Housing Fund (NHF): Where applicable, ensure your team is registered and contributions are managed correctly through the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN). Never assume a setup based on an employee’s previous job. Salary Records and Payslips: Issue an itemized payslip each pay cycle, detailing gross pay, statutory deductions, and net pay to ensure transparency for auditors and employees. Employee Records and Data Protection Creating records is only half of the work; how you store and secure them is the other half. Under Section 75 of the Labor Act, you are legally required to retain wage and employment records for at least three years after the period they refer to. Simultaneously, employee data management is strictly regulated by the Nigeria Data Protection Act. The Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) mandates that you only hold personal information as long as you have a genuine, explainable business or legal reason to do so. Confidentiality and access controls are non-negotiable here. You cannot leave employee files sitting around on an open Google Drive or scattered across unlocked office desks. Limit digital and physical access only to the specific people (like your HR lead or payroll manager) who need that data to do their jobs. Workplace Policies Every Employer Should Have Effective workplace safety and compliance mean having clear rules written down before you actually need them. Every business should document and communicate these six core policies: Leave Policy: Clearly outline annual leave days, paid sick leave, and statutory maternity leave entitlements, along with the process for requesting them. Attendance Policy: Define what counts as lateness, how absences are logged, and the exact steps taken when absenteeism becomes a habit. Payroll Policy: State pay dates, how you handle public holiday delays, and how you fix payroll errors. Code of Conduct: Set a clear, respectful, and professional standard for how people are expected to behave at work. Grievance Procedure: Give your employees a safe, transparent, and step-by-step path to raise complaints without fear of retaliation. Disciplinary Process: Document a clear warning system before termination. This protects you if a dismissal is challenged. Conducting Regular HR Compliance Reviews An HR policy written a few years ago is almost certainly a liability today. Tax frameworks shift, pension rules get reinterpreted, and data privacy enforcement is tighter than ever. If your documentation sits stagnant, your employee compliance numbers suffer first because nobody told your team the ground rules moved. Review your compliance regularly with these four steps: Run scheduled internal compliance checks against your active employee files. Update policies as soon as national laws change. articles.summary: Employee Management Employee Records Management in Nigeria: Best Practices for HR Compliance and Payroll Accuracy Oluwakemi Adesina August 31, 2026 When it comes to maintaining a compliant workforce, establishing a modern system for employee records management in Nigeria’s regulatory environment is no longer optional. A single missing contract, unverified tax ID, or misplaced pension record can instantly trigger costly penalties during a surprise government audit. Disorganized files mean payroll errors, missed remittances, lost employee trust, and heavy fines. This guide gives you a step-by-step plan to move from paperwork chaos to a records system that keeps you compliant and your payroll accurate. What Is Employee Records Management? Employee records management means organizing, storing, securing, and updating an individual’s professional data throughout their entire tenure with your company. It begins the moment a candidate submits their onboarding documents and continues long after their exit interview. Historically, HR records management relied entirely on physical paper files, but physical files are easily lost, vulnerable to damage, and highly difficult to audit. A modern employee records system relies on a cloud-based system, giving your HR and finance teams instant, secure access to vital information whenever they need it. What Records Should Every Employer Maintain? For a proper employee management system, you need to collect six key types of employee data: 1. Employment Contracts The foundation of the entire employee lifecycle. This includes the original signed offer letter, job description updates, promotion letters, and any signed amendments regarding compensation adjustments. 2. Identification Documents To stay aligned with standard employment practices and national labour guidance, you must verify who your team members are. Collect government-issued IDs, valid NIN, BVN for payment safety, and verified residential addresses. 3. Payroll and Tax Records This category acts as your primary defense during external financial audits. It must include TIN, specific State Internal Revenue Service registration details, and historic payslip summaries. 4. Statutory Benefit Details Accurate employee record keeping requires capturing verified PenCom numbers alongside valid NHF registration codes. 5. Performance and Leave Logs Keep records of performance reviews, warnings, sick leave, and vacation approvals. These prevent bonus and termination disputes. 6. Exit Documentation When someone leaves, close their file with a signed resignation or termination letter, clearance certificate, and final pay calculation. Why Employee Records Are Critical for Payroll Accuracy Payroll depends on your HR records. If your data is wrong, your payroll will be wrong. Document Type Direct Payroll / Compliance Consequence Regulatory Oversight Contract Amendments Prevents overpayment or underpayment of basic allowances Federal Ministry of Labour Tax ID (TIN) Records Ensures accurate PAYE deductions and prevents annual tax audit fines State IRS (e.g., LIRS) Pension PINs Avoids unremitted fund backlogs and heavy interest penalties PenCom Attendance & Leave Logs Calculates precise overtime pay and accurate proration for partial months Internal Payroll Controls HR Compliance and Record Retention Maintaining a pristine workspace isn’t just about aesthetics; it is about audit readiness. Regulatory bodies in Nigeria expect your business to maintain secure record-keeping practices that protect sensitive data and are easy to review. Under the Nigeria Data Protection Act (NDPA), your company acts as a data controller. This means you are legally obligated to protect your team’s personal details from unauthorized access. Leaving paper files sitting casually on open desks or sharing employee spreadsheets over unencrypted public networks can lead to massive liability claims from the NDPC. Also, records should not be deleted arbitrarily. While basic operational data should be updated constantly to maintain data accuracy, historical tax, pension, and contract records should generally be retained for a minimum of six years to satisfy the requirements of national tax laws and labour guidelines during retrospective audits. Best Practices for Digital Employee Records Switching to digital records? Use these steps to protect your business and get the most from your data: Set Strict Access Controls: Not everyone in the company needs to see what a colleague earns or look at their medical history. Restrict file viewing permissions strictly to authorized HR managers and specific payroll administrators. Centralized Records: Avoid a fragmented setup where contracts live in one manager’s email inbox, bank details sit in a spreadsheet, and performance reviews are buried on a hard drive. Use a singular, unified platform. Establish Automated Backup: Ensure your cloud infrastructure automatically backs up data across secure, redundant servers. This safeguards your intellectual property against sudden hardware failures or cyber threats. Leverage Employee Self-Service (ESS): Give your workforce the autonomy to log into a secure portal to update their own address changes, upload new certifications, or view historic payslips. This frees your HR team from tedious manual data entry tasks. Common Employee Record Management Mistakes Accepting Incomplete Onboarding Folders: Allowing a new hire to start working before they submit their signed contract or valid tax details creates an immediate compliance gap. Tolerating Duplicate Records: Having multiple digital profiles for the same individual across separate legacy systems leads to massive data quality issues. Not Updating Status Changes Promptly: When an employee resigns or shifts departments, failing to log that information on the exact day of the change directly distorts your active payroll accuracy. Weak Security Protocols: Storing sensitive corporate data using basic, easily guessable passwords exposes your business to devastating data breaches. articles.summary: UT Health East Texas Expands Access to Care with New Facility in Whitehouse wroberts Mon, 08/31/2026 - 12:04 WHITEHOUSE, Texas (Aug. 25, 2026) — UT Health East Texas is expanding access to high-quality healthcare with a new, state-of-the-art facility that is under construction in Whitehouse. The more than 11,000-square-foot clinic, located on Highway 110, is designed to meet the growing needs of families in southern Smith County. “This location is situated along a growth corridor in southeastern Smith County,” said Steven Cox, MD, UT Tyler School of Medicine Faculty Practice Plan President. “As our community expands, we remain committed to meeting the increasing demand for quality healthcare close to home. This investment ensures that families in this area have convenient access to the care they need, when they need it.” Located at 710 Highway 110 N., next to the Taco Bell, the facility will house six family medicine providers and feature on-site X-ray and laboratory services, offering patients a convenient, one-stop destination for comprehensive care. “Our goal is to make healthcare more accessible and convenient for the communities we serve,” said Jason Boyd, chief operating officer of UT Health East Texas Physicians. “By bringing multiple services under one roof, we’re able to streamline the patient experience and deliver timely, coordinated care closer to home.” In addition to treating illness and providing preventive annual wellness visits, providers at the clinic will offer a range of services, including joint injections and minor procedures such as stitches and wart removal. Walk-in appointments will also be accommodated as availability allows. “Primary care is the foundation of a healthier community,” said Dr. Michael Racs, DO, MBA, primary care medical director of UT Health East Texas Physicians. “This new clinic allows us to expand access to preventive care, chronic disease management and same-day medical needs for patients in Whitehouse and the surrounding communities. By bringing more providers and services to this area, we can help patients build lasting relationships with their care teams and receive the right care at the right time.” About UT Health East Texas UT Health East Texas provides care to thousands of patients each year through an extensive regional network that includes nine hospitals, more than 90 clinics, the Olympic Plaza Tower, 13 regional rehabilitation facilities, two freestanding emergency centers, regional home health services, an EMS fleet of more than 65 ambulances and four helicopters, and a comprehensive eight-trauma center care network, including the region's only Level 1 trauma facility. As a partner with The University of Texas System, UT Health East Texas is uniquely positioned to provide patients with access to leading-edge research and clinical therapies while training and educating the next generation of physicians and other health professionals.
articles.title: UT Health East Texas Expands Access to Care with New Facility in Whitehouse
